correctness.rationale: Stochastic Fubini and one-dimensional Itô kernel integrals recover the variance and cross-covariance; Gaussian conditioning gives the variance reduction c(t)^2/(v(t)+eta). At (t,eta)=(0,0), c(t)=O(t) and v(t) is of order t, so the extension by zero agrees with the deterministic observation. I independently verified the derivative -2QF/D^2 of Q^2/D, the cubic endpoint signs and the zero-noise factorization. For positive noise strict convexity and opposite endpoint signs force a single upward crossing, and the quadratic factor gives the unique crossing at zero noise. The zero-noise root exceeds sqrt(L); at y_infinity=sqrt(2L-1) the cubic is strictly positive, and F_T<0 below this point. These give the strict positive-noise shifts, monotonicity, and a bracket independent of noise, proving the stated uniform stiff limit on taking logarithms. For small damping the kernel error gives c_lambda(t)=t-t^2/2+O(lambda t) and v_lambda(t)=t+O(lambda t^2), with v_lambda(t) at least exp(-2 lambda)t; hence the gain converges uniformly even at zero noise. The Brownian gain has the displayed unique optimizer, so the argmax converges.
residual_risks: Uniformity here concerns large damping, not persistence of an information gain at infinite noise. The proof and not the cubic grid checks supplies the full parameter statement.

value.rationale: The one-reading scalar-integral placement has exact interior bounds and moves systematically with measurement noise in a zero-start Markov model. A uniform large-damping bound across noise regimes gives a genuine qualitative placement rule, and the Brownian limit connects two normalized Gaussian integral designs. This is a natural complete fixed-budget classification rather than a numerical instance.
residual_risks: No multisite or stationary-OU design follows, and the information gain tends to zero in the infinite-noise limit.
